pillar_reactions.evidence: He tied the functional-training premise to his own goal unprompted, before the pillar was formally presented: 'I'd not seen anyone specifically focused on kettlebells before, and I think I liked the idea of that in that it seems, you know, functional to me... perhaps just lending itself better to my goals on the functional side, and yeah, I've not seen anyone present that before, so it just grabbed my attention.' It is also what he opened the call asking for - 'just do the kind of strength building and movement, you know, that functionality side that I want'. When the pillar was actually delivered he had no questions ('No, I don't think so'), because he was already sold on the concept.

Understood and agreed with no questions: 'No, that's fine.' This was a stated draw for him earlier in the call - 'I guess I was attracted by the fact that, you know, there's the nutrition side mentioned, as well as, obviously, the workout program itself' - and it fills a real current gap, since he is self-managing nutrition after losing the PT who used to handle it. The rep presented it generically and never connected it back to the cut the prospect is actually stuck on.

Asked mechanics questions to understand what he would actually get: 'in terms of what you're getting for this, the support from Trevor, what's the availability on that? Is it a seven-day-a-week thing, or how does it work in that sense?' and then probed the composition of the community: 'so yeah, in the community, then there's a mixture of other...'. He had earlier confirmed accountability matters to him - 'the accountability is great as well because it's like, yeah, you aren't getting out of it... I would never let someone down' - so the interest was genuine rather than sceptical.

anchors.raw: I've been given details of a PT over in Portugal as well, which my current PT in Bristol has a friend basically in Portugal and he knows this PT over there. So, you know, that's where my consideration is of what do I want to do exactly.
anchors.competitor: An unnamed in-person personal trainer in Lisbon, Portugal, referred by his current Bristol PT
anchors.note: A live, warm, referred alternative he will speak to before deciding, and no price for it was ever established on the call. He explicitly framed the decision as a comparison - 'get the costs, speak to the PT as well, so I've got the comparison'. The rep never asked what the Portugal PT would cost or what it would cover, so he has no idea what number he is being weighed against.

anchors.raw: I've been training Cali for about six months. Previous to that, I'm doing that with a PT at the moment in Bristol. Previous to that, I was training with another PT in Bristol
anchors.note: Proposed label: established_habit_of_paying_for_coaching. He is on his second or third paid PT, currently four sessions a week, and has never questioned paying for coaching - only the delivery format. When $6,000 and $9,000 were quoted his entire reaction was 'Okay. That's fine.' This is the strongest supportive anchor in the batch and it went completely unused.

anchors.raw: in person is my preference... I don't think you can beat someone being there physically and keeping a closer eye. And, but, you know, there's, there's, there's a place for online as well.
anchors.note: Proposed label: delivery_format_expectation. The anchor in his head is not a price, it is the physical presence of a coach watching his form, set by a lifetime of only ever training in person. Everything he values is priced in his mind against that standard, and the rep agreed with the standard rather than reframing it.

unmet_demand.want: A coach physically present to watch and correct his form, which he describes as a perfectionist requirement.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is remote by design; form correction happens through video submission. The rep confirmed the limitation rather than bridging it: 'if you want to be there with somebody in person obviously that's not what this program is'.

unmet_demand.want: Continued coaching on calisthenics specifically, including learning new movements on that discipline.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The Kettlebell Body is built around the kettlebell movement library. He intends to keep a separate calisthenics coach for this, which permanently splits his coaching budget.

unmet_demand.want: To run the programme alongside an in-person PT rather than instead of one - he said he would do both 'without a doubt'.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing in the offer or the pitch positions the programme as a complement to existing in-person coaching, so the prospect was left to work out the combination himself and the rep framed it as an either/or.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that a programme built on loaded kettlebell work is appropriate while he is under physiotherapy for a deltoid injury.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised the injury and it was never picked up. Neither the programme's ability to work around a shoulder problem nor any clearance requirement was discussed, so a live clinical question sits unanswered underneath a decision he is about to make.
